title: The Value of Memory in Language Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.31303v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Memory enables language agents to carry useful distinctions from past experience into future decisions. Its value depends on which distinctions survive, whether a bounded agent can use them, and what can be recovered or revised as demands evolve. We develop a decision-theoretic framework that follows this value from raw history through persistent state, operational use, and costly recovery and revision. Original and retained value are expressed in units of avoided task loss; risk-cost frontiers describe attainable recovery and preservation across uses. Unknown demand yields value profiles, while interactive feedback changes the distribution of future work. A cost-aware simulation condition and five minimal counterexamples expose the roles of information timing, retrieval access, component interaction, feedback and demand uncertainty. translated_title: 语言智能体中记忆的价值
translated_abstract: 记忆使语言智能体能够将过去经验中有用的区分带入未来的决策中。其价值取决于哪些区分得以留存、有界的智能体能否使用这些区分，以及随着需求的演变哪些内容可以被恢复或修正。我们开发了一个决策论框架，追踪这一价值从原始历史到持久状态、操作化使用以及代价高昂的恢复与修正的完整过程。原始价值与保留后的价值以所避免的任务损失为单位来表达；风险-成本前沿刻画了在各种用途下可实现的恢复与保存能力。未知需求会产生价值画像，而交互式反馈则会改变未来工作的分布。一个成本感知的模拟条件与五个最小反例揭示了信息时机、检索访问、组件交互、反馈以及需求不确定性所扮演的角色。特别地，一个与答案具有零互信息的指针仍然可以降低精确恢复的成本。
tldr: 该论文提出一个决策论框架，以所避免的任务损失为单位，量化语言智能体中记忆从原始历史到持久状态、操作使用及代价高昂的恢复与修正全过程中的价值，并通过成本感知的模拟条件和五个最小反例揭示信息时机、检索访问、组件交互、反馈和需求不确定性对记忆价值的关键影响。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a decision-theoretic framework that quantifies the value of memory in language agents—in units of avoided task loss—from raw history through persistent state, operational use, and costly recovery and revision, and uses a cost-aware simulation condition plus five minimal counterexamples to reveal the roles of information timing, retrieval access, component interaction, feedback, and demand uncertainty.
